newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins stuck, expect freeze on stolen bond.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins stuck, expect freeze on stolen bond.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds were little changed on Tuesday as trading has largely stopped while the market waits for news about the possible freezing of another batch of bonds, dealers said.
Russian police are preparing an order to freeze up to a further $7 million nominal of MinFin bonds, which have been stolen.

"There is almost no trading and mainly because of the freezing news. Everybody wants the problem to be cleared up, and few operators are working given the higher operation risk," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.

Avtobank dealer Pavel Afanasyev said some banks were quoting prices but no deals had been struck even through brokers. "Even news that the next tranche of the IMF is likely to be paid has had no impact on the market in this situation," he added.
Economists said on Tuesday Russia seems to be broadly fulfilling the terms of its $10 billion loan with the IMF and the fund is likely to pay out the next instalment of the credit.
